fixes.explanation: Flip that one around, friend. The text says her eyes have "overcome" him, and ignored isn't the word. He says, "Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me." I think her eyes got to him, and that's why he asks her to look away.
Not that one, baker. The verse says, "Turn your eyes away from me, for they have overcome me." The word is overcome, not forgotten. I think her eyes hit him hard.

Right, baker. He says, "each has its twin, and not one of them is lost." Every tooth has its partner, and none are missing. It's like a cookie box where every cutter shape comes in a pair and not one is missing from the box.

Yes, baker! The text says, "The maidens see her and call her blessed…" They see her, and they call her blessed. That's a good word to get from a crowd, and mine usually just takes the cookies and runs.
No turning away here, friend. The verse says the maidens see her and "…call her blessed…" They see her, and what they do is call her blessed. Turning faces away isn't in the verse.
Not that one, baker. The maidens see her and "…call her blessed…" That's what the text says they do. Walking past her isn't in the verse.

Right, baker. The text says, "the queens and concubines sing her praises." So it isn't only the maidens who speak well of her. The queens and concubines do it too, and I think that's a lot of praise for one dove.

That's the word, baker. The speaker went down "…to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom." So the grove trip is about checking for new growth. It's like peeking in the oven to see if the dough is rising.

Harvested isn't the word, friend. The speaker went to see the blossoms of the valley, and to see "…if the vines were budding…" Budding is the word the verse uses. The speaker is checking for growth that's starting.

Withered isn't in this verse, baker. It says the speaker went down "…to see the blossoms of the valley, to see if the vines were budding or the pomegranates were in bloom." The speaker is looking for budding and blooming. Those are the words the verse uses.

Not quite, friend. The speaker says, "Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people." So the speaker didn't realize it beforehand. Knowing all along isn't what the text says.

Yes, baker. The speaker says, "Before I realized it, my desire had set me among the royal chariots of my people." The speaker didn't realize it before it happened. So knowing all along isn't what the verse says.
